title: Seljuk Empire
summary: The Seljuks, a Muslim Turkic clan of the Oghuz, rose under Toghril in 1037 and routed a Ghaznavid army at Dandanqan in 1040. By 1055 they held Iran and Iraq, and Toghril entered Baghdad as protector of the Abbasid caliphs. Turkish warbands pushed into Byzantine Anatolia, and Alp Arslan’s victory at Manzikert in 1071 began lasting Turkish dominance there. Seljuk power peaked under Malikshah; rule in eastern Persia ended with Sultan Sanjar’s death in 1157.

uncertainty.note: Dated from the rise of Toghril Beg in 1037 (confirmed at Dandanaqan in 1040) to the death of the last Great Seljuk sultan Toghril III in 1194. Main line rule in eastern Iran ended with the death of Ahmad Sanjar in 1157.

importance.justification: Brought Turkic rule to Iran and Iraq and opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement (R3 D3 T3 L3).

related.because: Sultan Alp Arslan's victory at Manzikert in 1071 broke Byzantine border defenses and enabled the Turkic settlement of Anatolia.
Turkmen nomadic migrations through Iran and Armenia into Anatolia expanded following the initial Seljuk conquests.
Seljuk expansion into Byzantine territories prompted the appeal from Emperor Alexios I Komnenos that led to the First Crusade.
